resolved_during_audit.title: LIGHT_BENCH harness timed JSON and cold allocations
resolved_during_audit.resolution: harness v2 at 46939bbe (solver call only, warm/cold allocations, spread reruns); v1 data marked superseded

refuted_sub_claims: SC-02 option 1 (stop treating quota-stopped batches as pressure): refuted as hazardous. The winning initial entries on stiff-forced, relaxation, stale-return and case5 fire on quota-stopped batches with only 2-5 rejections.

SC-02 cooldown sequence '4,8,16,32,64': the observed spacing after the initial pilot is 8,16,32,64 batches. The callgrind shares 88%/83% include the one-time coefficient parse; steady state is 87%/82%.
SC-03 '18% of pilot Ir outside the stepping loop': that share included the 511k one-time coefficient parse. Steady state is 7.1% on rotation and 4-5.5% on gyro.

SC-04 'monomorphized vs not' mechanism and the +7-11% wall-time win: both paths make one out-of-line RHS call. The wall deltas are within noise (user callback code itself is +5.5%). Only +1.2-2.4% Ir is reliable.
SC-06 for run() probes: the ExplicitSolution is consumed there (final_state, stats, stop_reason, callback_failure). Only the main tenure path discards it.
SC-07 risk class 'counter-changing': removing landings changes batch boundaries and therefore pressure, so it is policy.

CE-01 impact on rotation, gyro and case5 decisions: rotation and gyro lose even at h0=L/3 (1051 vs 154 WU), and the case5 pilot already starts at h0=L. CE-01's 'DOPRI comparator runs warm' is false for initial comparisons.
CE-01 'passes exactly when h_R* >= L/k_hat': the condition is approximate. Pass/fail is non-monotone in h0 (0.40452: L/3 gives 196 WU, L/2 gives 290 WU).
CE-02 Ir saving of 0.76M per solve: understated. It is about 0.9M (16%), and the 5.86M denominator included the parse.
CE-03 alternative 'arm the Guard with floor(rho*W_D) - solves_so_far': not buildable, because the Guard is armed once and solves happen inside the driver.
CE-04 '337 WU (55%) startup excess': the 193 explicit WU are productive work. The true excess is about 283 WU (46%).
CE-07 claim that one warm attempt suffices for the relaxation recheck: h_E_entry still needs 5 attempts, saving about 1. The structural bias against returns is unobserved in the registered cells.
MFK-05 as an independent counter-changing fix: it is n-JVP assembly by another route, carries the MFK-01 governance question, and is subsumed by MFK-01.
MFK-07 expected 2-4% gain from hoisting finiteness checks: it is under 1%. There is no separate jacobian-output pass in ShiftedOperator, only a single check at operator.rs:693.

MFK-08 'Arc::get_mut overwrite of captured state': not possible through Arc<dyn LinearOperator> or a closure-captured Vec. A new concrete operator type is needed. Also, MFK-08 is a known open item, not a new finding.
DFS-04 'all bitwise-safe': slimming Stats.options/y0 changes the public SwitchingSegment record (api/governance), and reusing the Guard needs a full per-batch reset.
DFS-05 location rodas5p_fast.rs:2502-2600: Workspace::attempt is at :1114, with stage loops at :1154/:1167.
DFS-05 SPD06 gain '16-26%': the same-binary ratios include legacy drift. The cross-binary figure is 12-26%, measured on the small driver only.

DFS-06 'half of step_to cost is call overhead' and the '25-40% landing-path gain' from inlining: the prologue was double-counted. Call overhead is about 15 Ir of 59 per call, at most about 3% of DOPRI Ir.
DFS-07 '123 Ir per callback' (understated; about 193) and its implication that the micro-fixes are meaningful: they recover only about 1-3%.
DFS-08 rotation '551 vs 20 allocations from window bookkeeping': about 230 of those come from MF probe facade calls. Window bookkeeping is about 300.

ACG-01 'registered cross-model reviewer never ran': the AGENTS.md Opus reviewer ran pre-execution, and the preregistration discloses it. The 'both checkers exit 0' closure test is unattainable because of 310 pre-existing repo-wide FAILs.
ACG-02 'cannot support a speed claim' as a new insight: PROTOCOL.md already states this. The ladder remedy is already registered (NEXT_STEPS.json:51-52).
ACG-05 proposed rejection-fraction admissibility gate: it would not flag the cited window (2.4% vs 0.3). A Hairer stiffness detector contradicts the documented design (switching.rs:3).
ACG-06 'reports attribute the gap to landing obligations': the packet states the measured scope includes output obligations; it does not attribute the gap to them.
ACG-07 '+58% endpoint error is material': 1.74e-8 against a 1e-5 cap is in the same band as direct DOPRI (1.52e-8) and RODAS (1.18e-8).
ACG-08 'effects of 4-12% are unresolvable under the rules' and the case5 host 'flip': the paired ABBA classifier cancels drift, and case5 lost qualification without a reversal in sign.
ACG-10 'committed evidence contradicts the PASS narrative': PREREGISTRATION.md:163-166 discloses the DIFFERS flags and their cause.

Code reading:

issues.title: Selection evidence misreports incomplete comparisons: lower-bound return wins are recorded as admissible same-window point costs, and incomplete pilots publish a near-parity comparator ratio
issues.impact:
Decisions are arithmetically sound, but the records mislead.
- Downstream consumers keyed on SwitchingEvidence count lower-bound wins as completed comparisons.
- Rotation pilots report comparator_work_ratio 0.984 and gyro pilots 0.932, although they covered under 0.05% and under 5% of the prefix.
- The contract test locks in the conflation.
evidence: switching.rs:1254-1263 calls qualified_work_preferred(&replay.record, &record, true, ...) for an incomplete replay. :784-795 builds the point interval as ObservedWork. :1305-1306 sets evidence = ExplicitCheaperOnSameWindow; only the decision string at :1299 differs
tests/return_sentinel_contracts.rs:267-270 asserts evidence == ExplicitCheaperOnSameWindow on the lower-bound path
OPUS_REVIEW.log MINOR (line 1228) asked for CostInterval{lower: W, upper: inf} plus a separate evidence variant; only the label was changed
switching.rs:1460-1465 computes the pilot comparator ratio as pilot WU / batch WU even for ceiling-stopped pilots (bench_bin rotation adaptive: cr 0.984)
issues.proposed_fix:
- Add CostEvidenceKind::ObservedLowerBound with the comparison arithmetic unchanged. Do not relax CostInterval::valid(); doing so changes decisions.
- Add a SwitchingEvidence::ExplicitCheaperThanSameWindowLowerBound variant, use it at :1305, and update the contract test.
- Report comparator_work_ratio as None, or as a rate-normalised value, when a pilot is incomplete.
- Add a measurement cell with a counterfactual true completion cost.
issues.acceptance_test:
- Decisions, f64 results and WorkCounters are bit-identical on all cells.
- The lower-bound fixture emits the new variant.
- Incomplete pilots report no point ratio.
issues.v2_recheck_or_critique_note: Pilots already carry ImplicitPilotIncomplete evidence when incomplete (switching.rs ~1480); only their comparator_work_ratio is misleading. The return lower-bound path records ExplicitCheaperOnSameWindow, contradicting that variant doc (switching.rs:283-285) and pinned by return_sentinel_contracts.rs:267-270. The lower bound is sound only under the determinism/prefix assumption (Opus review NOTE).

Policy change requiring preregistration; ideally done after R04, because cold-pilot margins currently measure the ramp (q is about 1976 on rotation).
- After a loss, add max(1, floor(log2(q*rho))) to the negative-comparison count, where q = (W_p/d_p)/(W_D/L), bounded by max_backoff_batches.

issues.proposed_fix:
Add a caller-authorized opt-in, e.g. Jacobian::jvp(..).allow_small_assembly(n_max), with n_max fixed in a preregistration. The existing ROUTER_DENSE_SMALL_MAX is 8.
- When n <= n_max, the facade build() supplies a jacobian_into that fills J column by column from n guarded JVP calls on unit vectors, charging n jvp units.
- Route those problems Dense through the existing allocation-free rodas5p_fast driver.
- Record a distinct provider identity, e.g. JacobianRecord::JvpAssembled.
- Keep pure Krylov as the default.
- MFK-05 (reusing the stage-0 Krylov basis when k=n) is the same assembly by another route and is subsumed. Pursue it only if assembly is refused on governance grounds.
issues.acceptance_test:
Preregistered same-quality comparison on case5 and gyro-tight.
- The opt-in arm reproduces the rodas-dense attempt and RHS counts exactly.
- Error stays within the registered bound.
- jvp_vectors = n per linearization.
- Allocations are zero after the first batch.
- Without the opt-in, t/y f64 bits and WorkCounters are identical to current.

The FD-dense numbers come from a direct Rodas5p::solve on an FD-declared problem, not from the selector.

issues.title: Entry pilots start cold at opts.h0, so pass/fail tracks the step-size ramp and prefix length rather than regime cost; transition entries are delayed
issues.impact:
Counterfactual replays:
- transition-39: entry would move from t=0.4676 to 0.4261, saving about 10.3-10.5k of 48.4k WU (21-22%).
- transition-79: saving about 9.8-10k of 34.9k WU (28%).
- stiff-forced: pilot cost 144 -> 54 WU.
- relaxation: pilot cost 72 -> 54 WU.
- No decision change on rotation, gyro or case5. Rotation and gyro lose by at least 6.7x and 27x even with h0 = L/3. The case5 pilot already starts at h0 = L.
evidence: switching.rs:1422-1427: pilot h0 = opts.h0.min(L).max(min_step). adaptive.rs:168 max_factor 5.0. Ceiling floor(0.8*W_D) at switching.rs:1430-1431
transition-39 losing pilots (segments 0/9/13/17/25/34/51/84): h0 = 1e-4, 4 attempts, 183-185 WU, ceiling-stopped
Replay at t = 0.4260973734585346: h0 = L/3 gives 2 attempts, 98 WU, PASS (ceiling 153.6); h0 = 1e-4 gives 196 WU, FAIL
`bench_bin transition-39 adaptive tenure 0.4260973734585346 0.625 3.274e-4` -> 8036 WU, against 12480 DOPRI WU committed over [0.4261, 0.4683]
stiff-forced ramp bound: ceil(log5(1 + 4*0.0082/1e-7)) = 8 attempts * 18 WU = 144 against a 154.4 ceiling. Replay with h0 = L/8 gives 3 attempts, 54 WU
Caveat 1: the h0 response is non-monotone. At 0.40452: h0 = 1e-4 gives 245 WU, L/3 gives 196, L/2 gives 290 (2 rejections), against a ceiling of 153.6
Caveat 2: the first DOPRI batch also starts cold from opts.h0, so initial comparisons are symmetric-cold
issues.proposed_fix:
Seed the pilot at h0 = clamp(L/k_hat, min_step, L), with k_hat = max(1, floor(rho*W_D/c_hat)).
- c_hat is the route's deterministic per-attempt work: s*(rhs + solve) + n*jac or JVPs.
- Cap the pilot's max_steps at k_hat.
- Register a rejection-aware margin, because one rejection exhausts k_hat = 3.
- Evaluate initial (symmetric-cold) and later (warm-DOPRI) comparisons separately, and consider applying the change only to the later ones.
- Seeding the tenure from the pilot's last accepted step instead of the mean is a separate policy change.
issues.acceptance_test:
Preregistered run:
- transition-39 adaptive total WU at most about 38.5k, and transition-79 at most about 25.5k.
- All endpoint caps met.
- decay, rotation and gyro WU and decisions within the registered non-regression bound.
- stiff-forced pilot at most 54 WU.
- Initial-comparison outcomes reported separately.

issues.title: Losing pilots run on after they provably can no longer reach the prefix within the ceiling; a reachability screen keeps decisions unchanged
issues.impact:
Rotation: saves 456 of 568 pilot WU and about 0.9M Ir per solve (about 16% of the 5.69M steady-state solver Ir).
The screen preserves decisions, because a stopped pilot could not have passed.
The gain on transition and gyro is small, and it largely disappears once R04 is adopted.

issues.proposed_fix:
Add a progress-aware stop hook in the RODAS driver; the Guard cannot see h_next, so it cannot live there.
- Before each attempt, compute m = floor((rho*W_D - W)/c_min).
- Stop when h_next*(5^m-1)/4 < remaining distance.
- c_min = s RHS + s solves, plus ft for non-autonomous problems and n for a dense Jacobian build.
- Fire only after at least one accepted step.
- Record the stop as an ordinary losing comparison, so entry_memory and backoff are unchanged.

Reset lu_chosen/lu_kind, faer_lu, w_dense, row_end/l_start/col_end, the Jacobian buffer, the GMRES/LS pools and the recycle scope. Reusing the Guard requires resetting every Guard field.
(d) Slimming Stats.options/y0 is api/governance, because Stats is part of the public SwitchingSegment.

issues.title: Selector output rows depend on 32-attempt batching, and landing cost is never separated from selection overhead
issues.impact:
Landings add only a small amount of RHS work:
- decay: +6 RHS (+6.2%)
- rotation: +12 (+0.23%)
- gyro-tight: +24 (+0.1%)
The remaining explicit-cell gap is per-segment machinery plus pilots (R06, R11).
Row times are an artifact of the quota rather than the user's problem: rotation returns 33 rows for 8 windows, transition-39 148, gyro-tight 129. Removing window landings would change pressure and pilot cadence, so it is a policy change with low value.
evidence: LIGHT_BENCH: decay RHS 103 vs 97; rotation 5263 vs 5251; gyro-tight 24427 vs 24403; gyro-default 6667 vs 6631
switching.rs:2015-2019: commit pushes reached_time for every batch; :542-548 session schedule = all window endpoints; explicit.rs:204-215: direct path uses [t0, t1]
Batch boundaries decide pressure: a window-ended batch with fewer than 24 attempts is 'uncompared' (transition-39 segment 4)
issues.proposed_fix:
- Add a dopri-observed8 control arm (bitwise-safe) so landing cost and selection overhead can be reported separately.
- api/governance: let callers pass an observation schedule to SwitchingSolver, and keep batch endpoints in stats.segments instead of t/y rows.
- Do not remove window landings without a preregistered policy review.
